units.translation: προχαιρέτω [let him fare forward], where before προχαιρέτω [let him fare forward] I indicated a lacuna, perhaps to be supplied with the words ὁ δ᾽ ἐκφυγεῖν οἱ δοκῶν [the one who thinks he has escaped], after rejecting the interpolator's words found in M, τὸ δὲ προκλύειν, ἐπεὶ γένοιτ᾽, ἂν κλύοις [but to hear beforehand, since it might happen, you would hear], about which I spoke in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. LXXXIX.
the one who thinks he has escaped
but to hear beforehand, since it might happen, you would hear
And indeed bracelets are at hand to be seen
with warm outpourings of soft water
Ἀἰ-δοῦ σὺ πρύμναν πόλεος [Revere the stern of the city]
guiding the helm at the stern of the city
which also seethes around the stern of the city
Revere the stern of the city
Did the sailor, fleeing to the prow, find from the stern a means of safety?
ship's mooring cable, i.e. ropes by which ships are tied to land from the stern
with the joining of stern cables
helmsman, one who sits at the stern
holding the helm, helmsman who sits at the stern
Improperly of a ruler (as πρύμνα πόλεως [stern of the city] is said)
lord and helmsman of this land
faulty for πρέμνοθεν [from the stump], which see
prematurely (πρὸ καιροῦ [before the proper time], as Phrynichus explains in Bekker's Anecdota p. 61, 18).
Πρῴ γε στενάζεις καὶ φόβου πλέα τις εἶ [Early indeed you groan and are full of fear]
Thus Brunck. Πρώγε πρ. M, πρώιγε a corrector, over βα a μ. recentissima scripto, i.e. πρό γε στενάζεις [before indeed you groan], as is in apogr.

Νᾶσοί θ᾽ αἱ κατὰ πρῶν᾽ ἅλιον [And the islands along the sea headland]
Σα-ρωνικού πορθμοῦ κάτοπτον [visible from the Saronic strait]
On the accent and usage, see the vocabulary in Thes. vol. 6 p. 2131.
the common sea headland of both lands
And the islands along the sea headland
On the accent and usage, see the vocabulary in Thes. vol. 6 p
prow, front part of a ship

For this is the correct spelling, attested by Etym. M p. 692, 25. 823, 20, and not rarely preserved in older manuscripts exhibiting πρῶιρα [prow], not πρῶρα or πρώρα, as is often written in more recent manuscripts: see Thes. vol. 6 p. 2132
Thus Porson for ἄηται. i.e. πάροιθεν καρδίας ὡς πρώρας [before the heart as of a prow], as Wecklein explains in Stud. Aesch. p. 7.
the prow before, looking at the way with its eyes
and before the prow the sharp spirit of the heart
